title: Broad Adsorption Of Sepsis-Related PAMP And DAMP Molecules, Mycotoxins, and Cytokines From Whole Blood Using CytoSorb® Sorbent Porous Polymer Beads
author: Maryann C. Gruda

steps_raw.instruction: In vitro blood recirculation setup
Purpose: To perform a small-scale experiment to determine adsorption of analytes by polymers in whole blood.
Materials and Equipment for Recirculations:
500 mL IV Bag (Vygon Item #CMS-9405)
2L IV bag (Vygon Item #CMS-9420)
4L IV bag (Vygon Item #CMS-9440)
Bovine Blood (Lampire Item # 7200800)
Female Luer lock fittings (3/32”) (McMaster Item #51525k292)
Male Luer lock fittings (3/32”) (McMaster Item #51525k142)
Female Luer lock fittings (5/32”) (McMaster Item #51525k294)
Male Luer lock fittings (5/32”) (McMaster Item #51525k144)
Peristaltic Dialysis Blood Pump (Fresenius)
Cha-seal wax for Hematocrit Tubes (Henry Schein Item #2277344)
Blood Filter (Henry Schein Item #5072400)
140mL Monoject Luer Lock Syringes (New Era Pump Systems Item #SYR-MJ140LLBX)
4mL EDTA Blood Collection Tubes (Henry Schein Item #2939187)
22 gauge syringe needles (Henry Schein Item #9879489)
10mL Luer Lock Syringes (Henry Schein Item #9874914)
Hematocrit Tubes (Henry Schein Item #1303223)
Streamline Blood Sets (Henry Schein Item #6669063)
Pediatric Blood Sets (Medisystems Item #B3-6605M6792)
Thermo Fisher Heraeus Megafuge 16R Centrifuge (CYT-0026)
Recirculation System Configuration
Peristaltic Blood Pump
Blood Filter Reservoir Outlet Luer Fittings In-line Sample Port
Reservoir Inlet Luer Fittings
Recirculation Set-up Procedure
Assemble column housing and fill device with CytoSorb polymer if applicable.
Obtain an IV bag and cut off the bag spike. Fix the cut tubing with a hose clamp. Attach a 3/32” female Luer fitting to the end of the tubing. Fill an IV bag with at least 500 mL of 0.9% saline.
Remove the blood filter from the packaging and cut the tubing 6 inches from the outlet of the filter. Make sure to move clamp so that it is positioned within 6 inches of the filter outlet.
Close the clamp, remove the spike cover from the filter and insert it into the outlet port of the saline IV bag. Hang the saline bag on a three-pronged clamp attached to a ring stand.
Attach a male 3/32” Luer fitting to the end of the blood filter outlet tubing.
For a large volume reservoir (up to 1L)
A female Luer fitting should be attached as the blood tubing does not need to be shortened.
Attach the red male Luer fitting on the peristaltic tubing to the female Luer fitting attached to blood filter.
Cut off the red fitting on the opposite end of the blood tubing as close to the fitting as possible.
For medium volume reservoir (0.3- 1L)
Remove blood lines from packaging and cut the tubing 12 inches short of the in-line sample port located next to peristaltic tubing.
Place a female 5/32” Luer fitting into the newly cut tubing and connect to the male 3/32” Luer fitting attached to the blood filter tubing.
Cut off the red fitting on the opposite end of the blood tubing as close to the fitting as possible.
For small volume reservoir (<0.3L)
Use an arterial side pediatric blood line, cutting the tubing such that 2 inches remain extending from the degassing chamber side and from the output side of the peristaltic tubing.
Place a female 5/32” Luer fitting into the newly cut tubing and connect to the male 3/32” Luer fitting attached to the blood filter tubing.
Open the clamp on the blood filter tubing to allow saline to flow. Move the tubing down to allow for the saline to flow until it begins to exit the open end of the tubing. Close the clamp.

Open the door to the peristaltic blood pump. Place the peristaltic tubing in the left side of the pump and spin the pump center as you position the tubing around the pump motor in an inverted U shape. Spin the fasteners at the lower part of the pump down to secure the peristaltic tubing.
Place an assembled CytoSorb column in a three-pronged clamp attached to a ring stand. The clamp should be positioned at least 6 inches above the ring stand base.
For small volume reservoir experiments:
Cut a piece of tubing 14” long.
If CytoSorb column caps used were Luer fitting caps, place a male 5/32” Luer fitting into the end of cut tubing. Connect male Luer fitting to the outlet end of device.
If the device caps used were hose barb caps, wrap the barb with Teflon tape and place tubing onto the barb on the outlet end of the device.
For large volume reservoir experiments:
The tubing marked by blue clamps included in the blood set should be used.
If the device caps are Luer caps, connect the blue Luer fitting before the air filter to the outlet end of device.

If the device caps used are hose barb caps, cut off the blue Luer fitting before the air filter, wrap the outlet barb on the device in Teflon, and place tubing onto the barb. Connect the other end of the tubing to the inlet Luer fitting on the saline IV bag. Secure air filter in a three-pronged clamp approximately 6 inches above the device.
Turn the device over 180° in the three-pronged clamp.
If the device caps are Luer caps, place a male 5/32” Luer fitting into the open end of the peristaltic tubing and connect to device.

At this step, if any saline has leaked out of the peristaltic tubing, run the pump momentarily to fully prime the line before connecting to the device. Turn the device over 180° so the outlet faces upward.
If device caps are hose barb caps, wrap barb in Teflon tape and place open end of the peristaltic tubing onto barb.

At this step, if any saline has leaked out of the peristaltic tubing, run the pump momentarily to fully prime the line before connecting to the device. Turn the device over 180° so the outlet faces upward.
Open all clamps along the flow route of tubing.
Set the peristaltic pump to recirculate saline through the device at 220 ml/min for at least three hours prior to the blood recirculation experiment.
Blood Transfer to IV Bag Set-up for specific volumes
140 mL Syringe with plunger removed
Blood Transfer (Small volume) Procedure
Obtain a 140 mL syringe and remove the plunger.
Cut a piece of tubing approx. 6 inches long and place a 5/32” female Luer fitting into each end of the tubing. Connect one fitting to the syringe Luer lock.
Obtain a 500-2000mL IV bag, depending on the desired reservoir volume.
Cut the bag spike off of the IV bag.
Place a clamp onto the cut tubing and place a 3/32” male Luer fitting into the end.
Connect the other end of the tubing from the syringe to the IV bag male Luer fitting.
Close the tubing clamp.
Obtain a filled blood bag and cut off the bag spike.
Open the clamp on the blood bag tubing and begin to fill the syringe with blood.
When the syringe is filled with desired volume of blood, close the clamp on the blood bag.
Open the clamp on the tubing from the syringe to allow transfer into the IV bag.
After all of the blood has transferred from the syringe close the clamp on the tubing.
Repeat steps # 9-12 until the desired volume of blood has been transferred to the IV bag.
After the desired volume of blood has been transferred to the reservoir bag, stop the saline recirculation pump.
Close the clamp on the inlet tubing of the saline IV bag and disconnect the Luer fittings.
Remove the blood filter from the reservoir bag used for saline recirculation, and place it into the blood reservoir bag spike port.
Blood Transfer to IV Bag set-up for large volume
Blood Transfer (Large volume) Procedure
Obtain a filled blood bag.
Remove the tab covering the bag spike entry point on the reservoir bag and insert the spike from the blood bag.
Cut off the spike on the recirculation IV bag and fix the tubing with a clamp. Place a 3/32” female Luer fitting into the open end of the tubing.
Open the clamp to allow the blood to flow from the blood bag to the reservoir bag.
Hang the blood bag above the recirculation IV bag to facilitate blood flow via gravity.
When the desired volume of blood has been transferred from the blood bag, remove the spike from the reservoir bag.
Turn off the blood pump on the saline recirculation setup.
Close the clamp on the inlet tubing of the saline reservoir and disconnect the Luer fittings. Remove the blood filter spike from the saline reservoir and place the spike into the blood reservoir bag.
Preparation and Administration of Analyte Spike
Obtain a 10 mL syringe with Luerlock fitting. Remove the plunger from the syringe and place a 3/32” female Luer cap to the syringe Luer lock fitting.
Using pipetters, transfer the desired volumes of analytes to the syringe. If the total volume of analytes is low (<1 mL) 1-2 mL of saline may be used to wash the analytes down the syringe walls.
When all analytes and saline have been added, replace the plunger back in the syringe body.
Invert the syringe so that the Luer cap is facing up and gently tap the Luercap to reincorporate any analyte back into the syringe body from the syringe tip.
Remove the Luer cap from the syringe Luer lock fitting and carefully push the plunger up so air is expelled from the syringe.
When as much air as possible has been removed, replace the Luer cap on the syringe Luer fitting.
When the analytes spike is ready to be added to the blood reservoir, invert the syringe again and gently tap the Luer cap to recombine any solution back into the syringe.
Remove the Luer cap from the syringe and replace with a syringe needle.
Pierce the membrane of the reservoir bag sample port and push the plunger in to expel the analytes into the blood.
While the syringe is still in the reservoir bag, pull out the plunger to fill the syringe with blood and push the plunger in to expel the blood back into the reservoir bag.
Repeat this step 3 times to ensure all analytes have been added to the recirculation IV bag.

If the blood recirculation being performed requires temperatures above room temperature, place the reservoir bag onto a heated water bag on an orbital shaker and allow the blood to mix for 30 minutes.

If the blood recirculation is being performed at room temperature and in small volume, the reservoir bag may be mixed manually by alternately tilting corners of the IV bag in a clockwise rotation for at least 15 minutes.
Recirculation Start Procedure
A T0 sample is taken directly from the reservoir using a 10 mL syringe with needle through the reservoir bag sample port.
Take hematocrit readings by placing heparinized capillary tubes down into the syringe opening.
While capillary tube is still in the syringe, place a finger over the top of the capillary tube.
Remove the capillary tube from the syringe and place into tube sealing compound while removing the finger from the top of the capillary tube.
Centrifuge the hematocrit tubes for 10 minutes at 1500xG.
Using a ruler measure the total length of fluids in the capillary tube, then measure the length of the red blood cells only. Record both of these values in a laboratory notebook.
Hematocrit values should also be obtained at the 300 minutes sample mark.
Push the plunger on the syringe to transfer the remaining blood sample into a 5mL collection tube.
Make sure all clamps along the recirculation flow path are opened except for reservoir bag inlet clamp.
Disconnect the Luer lock fittings at the reservoir bag inlet.
Hold the outlet blood tubing from the device over a 400 mL beaker and slowly start the blood pump.
Purge approximately 35mL of blood/saline for small volume, 75mL for medium volume, and approximately 150 mL for large volume recirculations.
Once the desired volume has been purged from the lines stop the blood pump.
Reconnect the Luer fittings between the device outlet line and the reservoir inlet line.
Turn the blood pump on and set it to 140 mL/min or other rate as required.
Use a timer to keep track of sampling times as soon as lines are reconnected for recirculation and the pump is started.
Sampling times are typically taken at 0, 5, 10, 15, 30, 60, 90, 120, 180, 240, and 300 minutes.
Samples taken after T0 are acquired from the in-line sampling port located before the peristaltic tubing.
Sample Preparation and Handling
Turn on the centrifuge.
Verify that the centrifuge relative centrifugal force (RCF) is set to 3000x gravity (xg).
Set the temperature on the centrifuge to 4°C.
Set the time to centrifuge samples to 10 minutes.
Immediately after transferring a sample into a blood collection tube, place the tube into the sample tube holder inside centrifuge.
Centrifuge the samples for 10 minutes at 3000xg.
Label two 2 mL flip-top micro centrifuge tubes for each corresponding sample time point.
Write the sample time, polymer identification number, date of recirculation, and notebook and page numbers onto each micro centrifuge tube.
Using a new 1mL transfer pipet for each sample, aliquot equal amounts of the plasma from the collection tube into two labeled 2 mL flip-top micro centrifuge tubes.
Label a cardboard sample storage box with the date, polymer identification number, the analytes spiked into blood, initials of personnel performing recirculation, and notebook and page numbers.
Place the sample storage box containing the samples into a -20° C freezer if available immediately after the samples have been aliquoted.

If a -20° C freezer is unavailable within proximity of the recirculation, samples may be placed into a refrigerator until the recirculation is complete and then moved to a -20° C freezer for long-term storage.
Scale Sizes Utilized in this publication
927mL* blood volume, 70mL CytoSorb device size, 140mL/min flow rate
265mL* blood volume, 20mL CytoSorb device size, 40mL/min flow rate
133mL* blood volume, 10mL CytoSorb device size, 20mL/min flow rate

*For 70mL polymer device, analytes are added to 1.07L of blood and 150mL are purged from the blood line to flush any residual saline, leaving a final volume of 927mL. For 20mL polymer device, analytes are added to 340mL of blood and 75mL are purged from the blood line to flush any residual saline, leaving a final volume of 265mL. For 10mL polymer device, analytes are added to 168mL of blood and 35mL are purged from the blood line to flush any residual saline, leaving a final volume of 133mL.
Preparation of Toxins, Administration, and Measurement

T-2 toxin (EnzoLifeSciences) in DMSO (30mg/mL stock) was diluted directly into bovine blood (Lampire Biologicals) to a final concentration of 10μg/mL, Aflatoxin B1 (Sigma) in DMF (10mg/mL stock) was diluted directly into bovine blood to a final concentration of 10μg/ml. Blood was recirculated through pediatric tubing coupled to a 10mL CytoSorb column at 20mL/min for 4hrs (T-2) or 5hrs (Aflatoxin) in the biosafety cabinet. Blood was then centrifuged for 10 minutes at 3000xg and plasma was collected for analysis, T-2 toxin was measured with the T-2/HT-2 Veratox Kit (Neogen) and aflatoxin was measured with the Helica Low Matrix Aflatoxin B1 ELISA (Helica BioSystems).
Preparation of Cytokines, DAMPS, and PAMPS, Administration and Measurement

IL-6 (Sigma) in H2O (100μg/mL stock) was diluted directly into bovine blood to a final concentration of 3000pg/mL, MIP-1α (LifeTech) in H2O (100μg/mL stock) was diluted directly into bovine blood to a final concentration of 400pg/mL, IFN-γ (Sigma) in 1% BSA-H2O (20μg/mL stock) was diluted directly into bovine blood to a final concentration of 400pg/mL, TNF-α (R&D Systems) in H2O (50μg/mL stock) was diluted directly into bovine blood to a final concentration of 800pg/mL. Blood was recirculated through standard blood tubing coupled to a 70mL CytoSorb column at 140mL/min for 5hrs on the bench top. Blood was then centrifuged for 10 minutes at 3000xg and plasma was collected for analysis. Plasma cytokine concentrations were analyzed by ELISA (R&D Systems).

C5a (R&D Systems) in H2O (50μg/mL stock) was diluted directly into bovine blood to a final concentration of 25ng/mL, HMGB-1 (R&D Systems) in 1X PBS was diluted directly into bovine blood to a final concentration of 100ng/mL, procalcitonin (Sigma) in H2O (100μg/mL stock) was diluted directly into bovine blood to a final concentration of 16ng/mL, S100-A8 (Acros) in H2O (100μg/mL stock) was diluted directly into bovine blood to a final concentration of 50ng/mL, SpeB (Toxin Technologies) in H2O (1mg/mL stock) was diluted directly into bovine blood to a final concentration of 100ng/mL, TSST-1 (Toxin Technologies) in H2O (1mg/mL stock) was diluted directly into bovine blood to a final concentration of 2μg/mL. Blood was recirculated through standard blood tubing coupled to a 20mL CytoSorb column at 40mL/min for 5hrs on the bench top. Blood was then centrifuged for 10 minutes at 3000xg and plasma was collected for analysis. Plasma was analyzed by ELISA for S100 and C5a (R&D Systems), procalcitonin (Sigma), HMGB-1 (Chondrex), and bacterial toxins (Toxin Technologies).
Preparation of B12, Administration and Measurement

B12 in H2O (10mg/mL stock) was diluted directly into bovine blood to a final concentration of 300μg/mL. Blood was recirculated through standard blood tubing coupled to a 20mL CytoSorb column at 40mL/min for 3hrs on the bench top. Blood was then centrifuged for 10 minutes at 3000xg and plasma was collected for analysis. A standard curve was prepared using un-spiked bovine plasma and B12 stock. A 500μg/mL high standard was prepared using 50uL of B12 stock and 1950uL of unspiked plasma. The high standard was serially diluted to standard curve concentrations of 250, 125, 62.5, 31.25, 15.625, and 7.813μg/mL, and a blank. 100uL of each standard and sample were pipetted to each well. The plate was then read on the Gen5 microplate reader (BioTek) at a wavelength of 550 nm.
